_what_this_is: the complete enumeration of what the pod CPU test gate refused, from pytest_outcomes.json — which the launcher pulled OFF THE POD before teardown via SessionSpec.setup_failure_files. Attempt 5's 99 skip identities died with the pod; this time all 113 survived, with the exact three-way set difference.

counts.note: the same 2922 tests were selected in both. The launch-bound sweep certified this exact tree at b82a2b13, 19 minutes of pod time earlier.

divergences.cause: STRUCTURAL, and caused by the recorder itself. Both skip when pe.RECORD_PATH is absent. record_pod_environment.py MOVES THE PREVIOUS RECORD ASIDE for the duration of the sweep — 'moved the previous record aside -> /tmp/podsim-record-*' — precisely so the sweep cannot certify itself. So during any launch-bound sweep the record is absent and these two SKIP; on any pod the committed record is present and they RUN.
divergences.generalisation: a sweep that hides an input to avoid self-reference guarantees a permanent skip divergence for every test that reads that input. This cannot be fixed by classification: the two machines genuinely differ, by construction of the measurement.
divergences.status: UNRESOLVED — needs a decision, not a waiver.

divergences.pod_skip_reason: declared host-local storage roots not on this machine: ['/home/ecs-user/aad-artifacts/', '/home/ecs-user/aad-scratch/']
divergences.cause: the paths are ABSOLUTE LITERALS IN docs/REPO_LAYOUT.md, read out of the Markdown. They are not located through Path.home(), so the CPU-test contract's fresh empty HOME cannot neutralize them: the dev box has them whatever HOME says, and the pod does not.
divergences.my_error: the skip-predicate registry gave the class `devbox_only_artifact` a single parity claim — 'reached either through $HOME or as a gitignored repo artifact' — and asserted it for every member. It is false for this member. A per-CLASS parity claim is exactly the excuse list the registry was built to avoid; parity has to be established per predicate, the way `path_parity` already does for the ones it can resolve.

divergences.cause: ATTRIBUTED, NOT PROVEN — see evidence_gap below. Every one of the 18 is in the single module that drives `simulate_pod_env.sh` as a subprocess, and that module PASSED on attempt 5's pod (2769 passed, 2 failed, both staging-contract). The only thing that changed is the CPU-test parity repair, which made the simulator shell out to `cpu_test_env_args.py`: `PODSIM_PY=$PODSIM_SCRIPT_DIR/../../.venv/bin/python`, falling back to `command -v python3`. A pod has no repo `.venv` — it uses /opt/train — so the pod always takes the fallback, which the dev box never exercises.
divergences.what_was_reproduced_at_zero_cost: the fallback is not a safe fallback. This dev box's /usr/bin/python3 is Python 3.6.8 and cannot even parse the emitter: `SyntaxError: future feature annotations is not defined`. That proves the fallback path is untested and interpreter-dependent; it does not prove the pod's python3 is what failed there.
divergences.status: UNRESOLVED, and the mechanism is unconfirmed.

evidence_gap.what: pytest_outcomes.json records skip REASONS but only failure NODEIDS — no failure messages or tracebacks.
evidence_gap.consequence: the pod named all 18 failures exactly and none of them says WHY, so the mechanism above is an attribution rather than a finding. The launcher's own window is `tail -40`, and the 18-line failure list plus the comparison block consumed it, so the pytest summary tail did not survive either.
evidence_gap.note: this is the same class as attempt 3R's four-line tail and attempt 5's missing skip list: each repair captured one more layer and stopped short of the next.

what_worked.evidence_off_pod: SessionSpec.setup_failure_files pulled /workspace/pytest_outcomes.json before teardown — 36,728 characters, all 113 skip nodeids with reasons, all 18 failures, and the computed set difference. Attempt 5's equivalent died with the pod.
what_worked.strict_comparison: it fired, named all three divergences exactly, and refused at $0.35 instead of after six trainings. This was its first real exercise on an L40S.
what_worked.cpu_test_isolation: the command-scoped contract did not leak: after the gate, on the real pod, `torch.cuda.is_available()` was TRUE again and the teacher cache was present at /root/.cache/huggingface/hub. That is the one claim that could not be proven on a CPU dev box, and it held.
what_worked.gpu_predicate: tests/autoinit/test_causal_depth_measurement_job.py::test_the_entrypoint_refuses_a_host_run_when_no_hardware_is_injected is NOT in either divergence list, so CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" did hide the L40S and it decided the same way on both machines.
